integrity: The proof derives the complete iterated-totient tail of 2^A 3^B exactly and reduces the target equality to 2^a=3^k+1. A parity split modulo 8 proves that the unique positive solution is (a,k)=(2,1). Bounded computation is used only as corroboration.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is restricted to primes whose predecessor has no prime factor other than 2 or 3. It does not settle the unrestricted existence problem for perfect totients of the form 3^k p with k at least 4. A relevant 2006 thesis was identified but its full text was access-blocked; only repository metadata and abstract were available.
title: No higher-\(3\)-adic perfect totients with a \(3\)-smooth prime predecessor
